items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: I got a chance to do some things for Decca Records, Gordon Jenkins, toward the end of '49... Whatever they needed; vocals mostly. Gordon Jenkins was sort of a house man there.

ctx.x: I think I got sick again in 1948 and while I was confined to bed and Benny called and wanted me to join him. I said I can't, I'm sick and he said, oh come on anyway. Meanwhile, I was still supposed to be doing things for Ray, but somehow he talked me into that and that let Ray off the hook. I never really went back after that; that was late '48. '49 I wasn't there any longer. Benny lasted about two weeks.

It just didn't work out. Then through '49 there wasn't very much there, except getting better. I got a chance to do some things for Decca Records, Gordon Jenkins, toward the end of '49. I thought I was going to get into the Decca crowd at that time, but that didn't work either. Then abruptly in '50 I got sick again.
